scope: Actual distinct-offset soft pair derivative and differentiation under an arbitrary integrable signed test; support for the mixed Gamma trace, not a hard coarea/trace/rate claim.

passages.correspondence: The actual distinct-offset derivative of F^(q+1)*pi_j in a_l equals((q+2)/h)*F^(q+1)*pi_j*pi_l for every naturalq and j!=l. The proof reuses the frozen actual power-offset derivative at q+1, times the genuine constant exp((u_j dot x-a_j)/h); j!=l proves its numerator is unchanged. This generalizes the printed second derivative identity and retains literal power/coefficient normalization.

For any measurable X and arbitrary integrable signed real test P on a probability space, the genuine soft offset derivative passes under its integral with no further hypothesis. Actual F,pi_j,pi_l belong to[0,1]. This derives primal integrability from normP and globally dominates the true derivative by((q+2)/h)*normP before applying dominated differentiation. The signed test remains unchanged; no hard-threshold derivative, coarea identity or final trace bound is assumed.

limits: Only h>0, distinct j,l and the displayed primal measure/measurable-X/integrable-signed-P assumptions are used. No normal-unit, moments of X, bounded P, density, coarea or desired trace comparison premise.
